description.short_caption: Axial brain MRI showing multiple ring-enhancing lesions.
description.detailed_description: This axial T1-weighted MRI with contrast demonstrates multiple ring-enhancing lesions scattered throughout the brain parenchyma. The lesions vary in size and are associated with surrounding edema. The findings are suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process, such as cerebral abscesses or neurocysticercosis. The image includes a scale bar for reference.

description.short_caption: Axial head MRI showing abnormal enhancement in the posterior fossa.
description.detailed_description: This axial MRI scan of the head demonstrates abnormal enhancement in the posterior fossa region, particularly involving the cerebellum. The image shows clear anatomical structures, including the orbits and sinuses anteriorly, with the cerebellum and brainstem posteriorly. The enhancement suggests a possible infectious or inflammatory process. The scan includes a scale marker for reference.
visible_findings: abnormal enhancement in the posterior fossa
clear visualization of orbits and sinuses

description.short_caption: AFB stain of scrotal tissue showing a single acid-fast bacillus.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of scrotal tissue stained with an acid-fast bacillus (AFB) stain. A single, slender, bright pink bacillus is visible against a pale blue background, consistent with the staining pattern of mycobacteria. The surrounding tissue appears lightly stained, with no other prominent organisms visible. The image highlights the diagnostic utility of AFB staining in identifying acid-fast organisms.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of scrotal tissue showing inflammatory infiltrates and granuloma formation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image shows scrotal tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes and histiocytes, with evidence of granuloma formation. The granuloma is characterized by a central area of necrosis surrounded by epithelioid macrophages and multinucleated giant cells. The background shows scattered inflammatory cells and stromal tissue.
